barred.how: every 32-hex-digit token and every 12-hex-digit world-id suffix in the text files under the roots (world files, truth, candidate tables, run records, tests); a seed is barred when it is such a token or its first 12 hex digits are such a suffix

definitions.D0_environments: E1 = the selection host with the selection's own Python environment: the reference program laid out as the task body holds it (its program folder), in this process, talking to the heat cell through the in-process transport (the wire's encoding and its program-time accounting), a fresh 256-bit token held in memory only; an observation tap reads the cell after every answered step and writes nothing. E2 = a throw-away container of the task image: the task's own verifier code runs the reference program restored as the submission, as the runner account under the verifier's limits and filters, in a fresh process over the cell's wire (the verifier's per-venue run with its one re-run after a cell failure). E3 = a machine with another CPU generation, the same pinned interpreter and library versions, in process, the token in memory only, nothing attached. Every run of one venue is one process; the compared environment variables are set and no OpenBLAS kernel variable is set.
definitions.D10_obs4_observable: OBS-4, observable. A patch that changes the plan is observable when, in the blind run (D12), over every pass of the patch (a run of ticks with a wheel ground point inside its polygon) in two windows, practice from its first tick to the forward timing crossing that completes its first lap (the mapping lap) and heat1 likewise (heat 1's run-up and first lap), one of two slip signals reaches at least 3 times its noise: lateral deficit = sign(kappa) (v_plan^2 kappa - a_y), kappa and v_plan of the blind run's plan of that session (practice: the track line's profile at practice_factor capped at practice_cap_mps; heat1: the race line's profile at race_factor, both planned on the world without floor patches) at the station of the car's reference point on that line, a_y = the mean of the tick's IMU lateral samples; slip speed = wheel speed less the true longitudinal speed. Noise = mean and standard deviation of the signal over the session's off-patch ticks between its first and last forward timing crossing: no wheel point in any patch, at least 1.0 s after the last tick that had one, not stopped, at least 3 s after a release; at least 20 such ticks. SNR of a pass = max over the pass and 10 ticks after it of |x - mean| / std; observable when the largest SNR over both windows and both signals is at least 3. A raised edge (all sides of one patch together) is observable when the largest pitch-rate SNR over its crossings in E1's practice window and heat1 window (as above, the first lap) is at least 3: IMU pitch rate at 200 Hz, sample j of tick n at (n - 1) x 0.025 + 0.005 (j + 1) s; base = samples in [t_c - 0.45, t_c - 0.05) s, at least 10; peak = max |g_y - mean(base)| over [t_c - 0.025, t_c + 0.15] s; SNR = peak / std(base).
definitions.D11_obs4_harmless: OBS-4, harmless when unknown: the blind run's whole day ends with end reason finish, every session has 0 crashes and 0 touches and neither heat has a contact bout with an opponent; or, failing that, the unknown-object run of that one object (D12) is such a day. Every patch that changes the plan and every crossed raised edge must be observable or harmless. Unknown-object runs are made only for the objects that are neither observable nor harmless by the blind run.
definitions.D12_blind_runs: The blind run is the reference program unchanged (its own parameters) for the whole day in E1 with the tap, except that its privileged world call is answered with a copy of the world whose floor has no patches (base grip, no raised edge); the cell keeps the true world. An unknown-object run is the same with only one patch removed (`<patch id>`) or only one patch's raised edge set to height 0 (`edge:<patch id>`). These runs are the per-venue observability check of the privileged reference program, not a pilot; no score is taken.
definitions.D13_recorded: Recorded without a line (E1's gate run): per heat and opponent, the beams of its marker box and of its silhouette in the car's first scan of the heat (on the grid); per overtake event of the heat records (time, opponent, kind), the car's centreline station and the track width (left plus right) there; per heat and pair of opponents with the faster one behind, the first session time at which, both on the track, the along-track gap from the follower's front (reference-point station plus 0.20554 m) to the leader's marker box rear face is at most the opponents' gap_keep_m (the start of a train).
definitions.D14_keep: Per cell the first candidate in drawn order that passes items 4 to 7; candidates are judged in drawn order and every judged candidate before the kept one is a rejection with its failed items and numbers; candidates after the kept one need not be run (listed as not needed, or, when they ran, as judged and not needed). A candidate that fails an earlier item is not run for the later items (recorded as not run).
definitions.D15_lap_check: The hidden set's N is checked against the lap range the agent's documents state for past venues; the check and the measured values are written to the hidden side only.
definitions.D1_candidate: A candidate is (cell, seed, order). Its base world is the venue generator's world for the seed, the cell's grip tier and layout class; its head-to-head world is the field generator's world for the base world and the tier in force (each heat's field drawn with attempt index 0 to 4 until it runs alone, item 4), first as a draft world (no lap count), then the final world with N (item 5). World ids follow the generators.
definitions.D2_item4: P1 the base world passes the shared world checker with 0 errors. P2 the model checker reports 0 errors for the base world's track model and for the heat model (the base world with that heat's field as its other cars) of each heat. P3 the class features of the venue generator's classes: Classic = duct gaps, exactly 1 open wall, 1 to 3 dust or metal-cover patches, no carpet tile, no shared wall, no section narrower than 1.2 m, no black duct; Featured = duct gaps, exactly 2 open walls, 1 to 3 dust or metal-cover patches, at least one carpet tile and at most 3 patches, exactly one shared wall, a section narrower than 1.2 m, black ducts making 12 % to 30 % of the outer wall; and the venue sheet's features equal the checker's expected features. P4 the generator's kinematic lap passes. P5 regeneration in a fresh process is byte-identical: the base world generated again in a new interpreter, and the whole draft world (base world, field draws and every field-alone run that chooses the attempt indices) generated again in another new interpreter, equal the first files byte for byte. P6 the world additions pass their checker with the deep check (the field and the grid redrawn from the base world, the tier and the recorded attempt indices, byte for byte), which also runs the path check of each of the six field lines and checks the grid's construction. P7 the grid predicates: in each heat every wheel point of the car's slot is at least 0.15 m inside the track, the four slot footprints are at least 0.5 m apart, no slot lies on a raised patch edge. P8 each of the six field lines passes the path check (wall clearance and smallest radius; part of P6, reported on its own). P9 each pace lies within 0.02 of its nominal, fastest first. P10 field alone: the generator's record shows, for each heat, a draw with attempt index 0 to 4 whose field ran 300 s alone without touching a wall or another car and without a staff reset, the first passing index being the one recorded in the world file; a heat with five failing draws makes the venue no candidate.
definitions.D3_item5: The lap-count run is one E1 run on the draft world (no heat ends on laps, both run to 300 s). Laps at 240 s of a heat = the number of the car's completed laps with lap end time at or before 240.0 s session time. N = the smaller of the two heats' laps at 240 s. N from 5 to 20: the final world is the draft world with N on its venue sheet and its layout digest renewed; otherwise the candidate fails item 5 and is not run further.
definitions.D4_item6: Gate runs: one run of the final world in each of E1 (with the tap), E2 and E3. REF-1 per environment: in practice and both heats the session's touches, crashes, pick-ups, out-of-bounds and warnings are 0; in both heats no contact bout with any opponent, no stop and K = 0; the venue result ends with end reason finish, 0 forbidden calls; the result passes the cell's record checker with 0 errors; the program ended without an error. REF-2 per environment: in both heats the car is classified, beaten is 3, C >= 5. REF-3 per environment: in both heats the heat ended on laps, ended by the car, and the car's N-th lap ends at or before 240.0 s. REF-4 per environment: in both heats every opponent's staff resets and wall touches are 0. REF-5: per heat the car's lap count, the heat's end reason and end time (its tick), the list of overtake events (time, opponent, kind, clean, reason), C, K, the session's warnings and each opponent's beaten flag are identical in E1, E2 and E3; whether the whole venue results without wall-clock fields are identical is reported. REF-6 per environment: every session's program time is within its cap and every desk time within its cap (the cell configuration's caps). The reference numbers are E2's: C_ref = each heat's C, T_N = each heat's N-th lap end time. Every environment that did not run, or ran with an error, fails REF-1.
definitions.D5_beams: A beam returns from an object when its scan value is non-zero (the LiDAR's returned flag) and the first surface along it is a LiDAR geom of that object: a duct piece's lidar geom; an opponent's marker box (its tail box lidar geom); for the silhouette, every lidar geom of that opponent. The count of an object in a scan is the number of such beams of that tick. The scan origin is the mean of the tick's sub-scan origins; distances are horizontal.
definitions.D6_obs1: OBS-1: the mapping lap is the whole practice session of E1's gate run (the run-up, the reference's timed lap at its mapping cap, the stop). Per duct piece the largest count over the practice scans; every piece at least 8.
definitions.D7_obs2: OBS-2: the two duct-end pieces of an open wall [A, B] are the last piece of A and the first piece of B. A practice scan of E1's gate run is within 3 m of an end when its origin is at most 3.0 m from that end's end-face centre. Per end the largest count of its piece over those scans (0 when there is none); at least 8.
definitions.D8_obs3: OBS-3, in both heats of E1's gate run. Along-track gap to opponent j at a tick = the station of j's marker box rear face (its reference-point station less 0.22292 m) less the station of the car's foremost point (its reference-point station plus 0.20554 m), wrapped to (-L/2, L/2]; stations are the track's centreline stations of the reference points. The opponent ahead at a tick = the opponent on the track with the smallest positive gap (behind a train of opponents this is the train's last car). An approach of j = a tick t_b at which j is the opponent ahead with gap <= 1.5 m, the car moving (ground speed > 0.05 m/s) and not stopped by its staff, and whose previous tick had j's gap > 1.5 m or j not ahead, such that before t_b there is a tick t_a of the same session with j's gap > 3.0 m and j's gap in (1.5, ...] at every tick between t_a and t_b, the car not stopped by its staff in [t_a, t_b] (t_a = the last such tick before t_b). A visible stretch of j = at least 10 consecutive scans with at least 5 beams from j's marker box each. A stretch counts for an approach when it overlaps [t_a, t_b] and j is ahead of the car (gap > 0) at the stretch's first scan. Margin at the stretch's first scan: need = v^2 / (2 a) + 0.5 m with v the car's ground speed then and a = the reference program's braking capability brake_frac_of_grip_g x race_factor^2 x mu x 9.81, mu the smallest true floor grip under the car's four wheel ground points at that scan; it holds when the gap then is at least need. Every approach must have a counting stretch whose margin holds. A heat without an approach passes OBS-3 trivially (recorded).
definitions.D9_obs4_consequential: OBS-4, which objects: the reference's heat plan = the reference program's planner on the world as built, its race line (bounds kept race_wall_clear_m from the walls) and that line's speed profile at race_factor. A floor patch changes the plan when, on a copy of the world whose floor lacks that patch (polygon, grip and raised edge), the same line's profile at the same factor is more than 2 % faster (v_without / v_with > 1.02) at some line sample at which one of the planner's four wheel points lies inside the patch's polygon. A raised patch edge the line crosses = a side (vertex k to k + 1) of a patch with edge height > 0 crossed by a wheel ground point of E1's gate run in heat1 or heat2 (straight path between two consecutive tick-end poses shorter than 0.5 m; crossings of one side within 0.5 s are one event).

crash_line_rule.text:
CRASH-LINE RULE. The line at which a contact with an opponent becomes a car crash starts at 0.18 m of lateral push.
PUSH. At the first contact of a bout the whole simulation is copied and the car is taken out of the copy; the copy
runs for 1.5 s, in which the opponent, the other two field cars and the track objects go on from their states at that
moment under the same driver. The push is the largest difference, within the 1.5 s after the first contact, between
the opponent's lateral offset from its own line in the heat and its offset in the copy at the same place on that line.
1. UNDISTURBED MOTION. Every field car of both heats of every development venue runs from the grid without the car for
300 s; u = the largest push, measured in the same way from copies taken at 30 s, 60 s and so on to 270 s of each run,
over all cars of the heats that pass the field-alone test of the selection rule (a heat that fails it is no
candidate's heat). 2. CONTACTS. At least 60 contact bouts between the car and an opponent are collected on the
development pool, with the field tier in force, through the heat referee of this task, from a program that exists for
other reasons: the reference program of this task with a lateral or timing error of known size put into it. For each
bout the push is measured as defined. 3. THE LINE STANDS when 0.18 >= 2 u and no measured bout has a push in [0.16,
0.20] m. 4. OTHERWISE the line moves to the middle, rounded to 0.01 m, of the widest interval inside [0.10, 0.35] m
that holds no measured push, lies at or above 2 u and is at least 0.04 m wide. 5. If no such interval exists, the line
is not set by this rule: the measurement is reported and the criterion is replaced only by a dated decision of the
lead designer taken before any candidate of the hidden set is run. 6. The numbers of items 1 and 2 are recorded
whatever the outcome; no bout is dropped.

lap_rule.text:
LAP RULE. The number of laps N of a venue's heats is fixed before any gate run. 1. LAP-COUNT RUN. On the venue's world
without N, the privileged reference program drives the whole day once with the lap target switched off, so that both
heats run to 300 s (selection host, in process). 2. N = the smaller, over the two heats, of the number of laps that
run had completed at session time 240.0 s. 3. A venue with N below 5 or above 20 is not a candidate. 4. N is written
on the venue sheet and the layout digest is taken over the world with N. Every later run uses that world. 5. CHECK. In
every gate run the reference completes its N-th lap at or before 240.0 s in both heats and is the car that ends the
heat; the reference program reads N only to know when a heat is over, so a gate run repeats the lap-count run up to
that moment.

selection_rule.text:
SELECTION RULE. 1. CELLS AND CANDIDATES: 6 cells = grip tier (low 0.45-0.55, mid 0.60-0.75, high 0.80-0.95) x layout
class (Classic, Featured), one venue per cell. Eight fresh os.urandom(16) seeds per cell (48), in drawn order 0 to 7;
a seed is used in exactly one cell. Barred: every seed of the earlier task's hidden set, of its candidates and reserve
candidates, of its development and rehearsal pools, of example and demonstration venues, and of this task's
development pool. 2. WRITE FIRST: the rule texts (tier, lap, crash-line and this rule), the tier in force, the cells,
the seeds with their order, the table of barred seeds by digest and the sha256 table of item 3 are written to the
selection record before the first candidate world is generated; a read-only copy of that record is kept. 3. FROZEN BY
SHA256 AT THAT MOMENT: the venue generator and the field generator with their parameters; the opponents' driver and
its parameters; the checker and constants; the cell (car, sensors, ducts, referee and heat referee with their
parameters and the grader configuration, wire, client library); the scoring module; the reference program; the
selection and observability scripts; recorded besides: interpreter and library versions, the verifier image digest,
the CPU models of the three environments. 4. GENERATOR PREDICATES (recorded per candidate): the base world passes the
world checker and the model checker with 0 errors and has the complete features of its class; the kinematic lap
passes; regeneration in a fresh process is byte-identical; the world additions pass their checker; every wheel point
of the car's grid slot is at least 0.15 m inside the track and the four slot footprints are at least 0.5 m apart; each
of the six field lines passes the path check; each pace lies within 0.02 of its nominal; FIELD ALONE: in each heat the
three field cars, run from the grid without the car for 300 s, touch no wall and no other car and need no staff reset;
a heat whose field fails this test is drawn again, the lines and the paces of its three cars, from the same streams
extended by an attempt index 1 to 4, with the driver, its parameters and the test unchanged, and the first draw that
passes is the heat's field; when all five draws of a heat fail, the venue is not a candidate; the attempt index of
each heat is recorded in the world file. 5. LAPS: N by the lap rule; 5 <= N <= 20. 6. REFERENCE GATES, each candidate
in drawn order, run once in three environments (E1 selection host, in process; E2 the verifier image, the program in
its own process over the wire under the verifier's account and filters, the reference numbers are taken here; E3 a
machine with another CPU generation, in process, the token in memory only): REF-1 clean day: in practice and both
heats touches, crashes, pick-ups, out-of-bounds and warnings are all 0, no contact with any opponent, the run ends
normally, 0 forbidden calls, the result passes its checker; REF-2 terms complete: in both heats the reference is
classified, all three opponents are beaten, and C_ref >= 5; REF-3 time: in both heats the reference completes its N-th
lap at or before 240.0 s and is the car that ends the heat; REF-4 field undisturbed: no opponent is reset by its staff
and no opponent touches a wall during the reference's day; REF-5 environments agree: per heat the lap count, the end
reason and its tick, every overtake event with its credit, C_ref, the warnings and the beaten flags are identical in
E1, E2 and E3 (bit-identity of the whole record without wall-clock fields is reported); REF-6 the reference is a legal
entry: program time within the budget of every session, desk times within their caps. 7. OBSERVABILITY (E1, made with
the reference, written to the review record; all must hold): OBS-1 every duct piece returns at least 8 beams in at
least one scan of the reference's mapping lap; OBS-2 each of the two duct-end pieces of every open wall returns at
least 8 beams in a scan taken within 3 m; OBS-3 every approach: each time the reference, moving, closes from more than
3 m to within 1.5 m behind an opponent or behind a train of opponents, the marker box of that opponent (of the last
car of the train) returns at least 5 beams in each of at least 10 consecutive scans, and at the first of those scans
the along-track gap to it is at least the reference's braking distance at its speed then plus 0.5 m; OBS-4 every floor
patch that changes the reference's plan and every raised patch edge its line crosses is either observable (a signal of
at least 3 times its noise in the mapping lap or in the first lap of heat 1) or harmless when unknown (the reference,
not knowing it in its plan, has a day without crash and without touch); recorded without a line: the beams each
opponent's marker box returns to the car on the grid, the stations and track widths of the reference's overtakes, the
times at which trains form. 8. KEEP: per cell the first candidate in drawn order that passes items 4 to 7; every
rejection is recorded with the failed item and its numbers; if all eight of a cell fail, that cell stays empty and the
measurement is reported: a further block of seeds needs a dated amendment written before those seeds are drawn; rule
and lines never change after the freeze; a defect in frozen code means a dated amendment and a restart from item 1
with new seeds for all cells; no candidate is kept or dropped on the score of any non-privileged program. 9. REPORTED
BESIDES: per cell the reason of every rejection and the track width and length of kept against rejected candidates,
because the gates favour wide venues where overtaking is easy; the features the six kept venues share that a program
could assume without looking. 10. FROZEN AFTER SELECTION (sha256): the six world files with their layout digests, the
six reference records (N, C_ref of both heats, the time of the N-th lap), the anchor (the reference's measured score
in one full verify in E2), the observability record, the completed selection record, the sha256 of the reference's
token; the verifier compares the layout digest at every venue; a repository-level test guards the hashes. 11. AFTER
SELECTION: the grader QC programs run on the six venues; validation: untouched 0.0, reference 1.0.

tier_rule.text:
TIER RULE. 1. TIERS. Three fields are registered. Each has three cars; a car's pace is a fraction of the reference
speed of its own line. Nominal paces by grid slot 1, 2, 3: fast 0.80 / 0.75 / 0.70; mid 0.80 / 0.70 / 0.60; slow
0.70 / 0.60 / 0.50. A car's pace in a heat is its nominal plus 0.001 n, with n drawn uniformly from the integers -20
to 20. The opponents' driver and its parameters are used as they are in every tier. 2. DEVELOPMENT POOL. 24
development venues, four per cell (grip tier low, mid, high x layout class Classic, Featured), fixed before the first
reference run of this task. Their seeds never enter the hidden set. No venue of the pool is replaced or removed; a
venue whose field cannot run alone (rule D item 4) counts as not passing. 3. A VENUE PASSES A TIER when the privileged
reference program, driving the whole day once on that venue with that tier's field, has in both heats: no contact with
anything (0 touches), no warning, no stop; all three opponents beaten (each overtaken cleanly at least once more than
it re-overtook, and behind at the end); a clean overtake balance C_ref of at least 5; and its N-th lap completed at or
before 240.0 s as the car that ends the heat, N by the lap rule. 4. DECISION. The task uses the fastest tier at which
at least 18 of the 24 development venues pass. The fast tier is tried first. Work on the reference program for the
fast tier ends at 9 lane-hours in all; if the fast tier has not passed by then, the mid tier is measured with the
program as it stands, with at most 1.5 further lane-hours of fixes, then the slow tier in the same way. If the slow
tier does not pass, the build stops and the owner decides. 5. FIXED. No line of item 3, no pace and no count is
changed after a result. The full-marks margin of the score is not widened to make a tier pass. The pace range told to
the entrant is the tier's lowest nominal minus 0.05 to its highest nominal plus 0.05.
